title: Wumpus world
summary:
Wumpus world is a simple world used in artificial intelligence for knowledge representation and reasoning. It was introduced by Michael Genesereth and is discussed in the Russell-Norvig book Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach. It draws inspiration from the 1973 video game "Hunt the Wumpus" by Gregory Yob.

The Wumpus world is a 4x4 grid consisting of 16 rooms. The agent starts at Room [1,1] facing right, and its goal is to retrieve treasure while avoiding hazards such as pits and the Wumpus. If the agent steps into a pit, it falls and dies; a breeze in adjacent rooms suggests nearby pits. The Wumpus is a creature that kills the agent if it enters its room; rooms next to the Wumpus have a stench, and the agent can use an arrow to kill the Wumpus. Glitter indicates gold in the current cell.

The environment is partially observable (the agent perceives only clues from adjacent cells and must infer hidden dangers using logical reasoning), deterministic (actions have predictable outcomes), static (the Wumpus and pits remain stationary), and discrete (the agent moves step by step through distinct cells).

The Wumpus World is a classic example used in artificial intelligence to demonstrate the capabilities of knowledge-based agents. It allows the application of many different types of AI techniques, including symbolic AI and logical-based AI for implementing predicate and first-order logic to calculate likelihoods of conditions within each room. It serves as an excellent pedagogical tool for teaching AI concepts, enabling students and researchers to experiment with intelligent behavior in uncertain environments.
